literal: Qiu Dui first guarded the baggage train at Anding; hearing that Xi Jin was defeated, he cast off armor and fled east to Puban.
idiomatic: Qiu Dui had been guarding the baggage at Anding; when he heard Xi Jin was beaten, he threw off his armor and fled east to Puban.

literal: The Emperor heard and was greatly angry; an edict that An Gu was to execute Qiu Dui.
idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered An Gu to execute Qiu Dui.

literal: Summer, fourth month: Helian Ding sent envoys with tribute; the Emperor issued instructions to him.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Helian Ding sent tribute; the emperor sent him a written reply.

literal: Day renzi: toured west.
idiomatic: On the renzi day the court toured west.

literal: Day wuwu: hunted on the west of the river.
idiomatic: On the wuwu day he hunted west of the river.

literal: General amnesty throughout the realm.
idiomatic: He granted amnesty to the empire.

literal: King of Southern Qin Yang Xuan sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Yang Xuan, King of Southern Qin, sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Sixth month, day dingyou: Bingzhou Hu chieftain Bu Tian plotted rebellion and was executed; the remainder were unsettled.
idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the sixth month Bu Tian, Hu chieftain of Bingzhou, plotted rebellion and was put to death; his followers were uneasy.

literal: An edict that Duke of Huainan Wang Beijin was to garrison Lüsi and comfort them.
idiomatic: He ordered Wang Beijin, Duke of Huainan, to garrison Lüsi and reassure them.

literal: Day jiayin: traveled to Changchuan.
idiomatic: On the jiayin day he went to Changchuan.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the court returned to the capital.

literal: Eighth month: toured east to Guangning and viewed the hot springs.
idiomatic: In the eighth month he toured east to Guangning and visited the hot springs.

literal: With the great offering he sacrificed at the temples of the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun.
idiomatic: He offered the great sacrifice at the temples of the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun.

literal: Rouran Datun sent his son with more than ten thousand horsemen into the frontier.
idiomatic: Datun of the Rouran sent his son with more than ten thousand horse across the border.

literal: The matter is fully set forth in the Rouran treatise.
idiomatic: The full account is in the treatise on the Rouran.

literal: Jinyai, chieftain of the Xiutu Hu of Shang commandery, led his tribe inward in submission.
idiomatic: Jinyai, Xiutu Hu chieftain of Shang commandery, led his people to submit.

literal: Ninth month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: In the ninth month the court returned to the capital.

literal: Quan Wu and others of the Ba chieftains of Shangluo, more than ten thousand households, submitted inward.
idiomatic: Quan Wu and other Ba chiefs of Shangluo, more than ten thousand households, came in submission.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day jiachen: toured north.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the jiachen day, he toured north.

literal: Day renzi: hunted at Niuchuan.
idiomatic: On the renzi day he hunted at Niuchuan.

literal: Wang Zhongde, frontier general of Liu Yilong north of the Huai, sent more than two thousand foot and horse to raid Jiyang and Chenliu.
idiomatic: Wang Zhongde, Liu Yilong's general north of the Huai, sent more than two thousand foot and horse to raid Jiyang and Chenliu.

literal: That month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: That month the court returned to the capital.

literal: Intercalary month, day xinsi: Yilong again sent Generals Wang Xuemo and Yanzhou Inspector Zhu Lingxiu with two thousand foot and horse to raid Xingyang, intending to strike Hubao.
idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the xinsi day, Yilong again sent Wang Xuemo and Zhu Lingxiu, governor of Yanzhou, with two thousand foot and horse against Xingyang, meaning to take Hubao.

literal: Yuzhou sent troops to meet and attack and drive them off.
idiomatic: Yuzhou sent troops to meet them and drove them off.

literal: Kui Zhi, chieftain of the Tuge of Shang commandery, led more than ten thousand households inward in submission.
idiomatic: Kui Zhi, Tuge chieftain of Shang commandery, led more than ten thousand households to submit.

literal: Xianyu Taiyang, Zhai Qiao, and others of the Dingling at Dingzhou, more than two thousand households, rebelled into the western hills, plundering commanderies and districts; the provincial army campaigned against them and was defeated.
idiomatic: At Dingzhou, Xianyu Taiyang, Zhai Qiao, and other Dingling, more than two thousand households, rebelled into the western hills and looted the districts; the provincial army attacked and lost.

literal: An edict that General Who Guards the South, Marquis of Shouguang Shusun Jian, was to attack them.
idiomatic: He ordered Shusun Jian, General Who Guards the South and Marquis of Shouguang, to strike them.

literal: Eleventh month: traveled to Hexi and held a great hunt.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month he went to Hexi for a great hunt.

literal: Twelfth month, day jiashen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the twelfth month the court returned to the capital.

literal: That year the imperial son Huang was born.
idiomatic: That year the prince Huang was born.

literal: Qifu Chipo died; his son Mumi presumptuously succeeded.
idiomatic: Qifu Chipo died and his son Mumi seized the throne.

literal: Juqu Mengxun sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Year 2, spring, first month: Helian Ding's younger brother Duke of Jiuquan Jun came in flight from Pingliang.
idiomatic: In the second year, first month of spring, Ding's brother Jun, Duke of Jiuquan, fled from Pingliang to the court.

literal: Xianyu Taiyang and others pleaded guilty; an edict pardoned them.
idiomatic: Xianyu Taiyang and his band pleaded guilty and were pardoned.

literal: Second month: Li Yu of Shangdang gathered a host, killed the governor, styled himself King Without Superior, and appointed generals.
idiomatic: In the second month Li Yu of Shangdang raised a force, killed the governor, called himself King Without Superior, and set up commanders.

literal: The defending general of Henei attacked and defeated him.
idiomatic: The garrison commander of Henei defeated him.

literal: Yu fled into the mountains; men seized him and sent him in; he was beheaded.
idiomatic: Yu fled into the hills, was seized and sent in, and was beheaded.

literal: Summer, fourth month: troops were drilled at the southern suburb.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer the army was drilled at the southern suburb.

literal: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Day gengyin: the imperial carriage campaigned north; Grand Commandant, Prince of Beiping Changsun Song, and Commandant of Guards, Duke of Guangling Lou Fulian, were left to guard the capital; by the eastern route he was to join Changsun Han and others at the enemy's court.
idiomatic: On the gengyin day the emperor marched north, leaving Changsun Song, Grand Commandant and Prince of Beiping, and Lou Fulian, Commandant of Guards and Duke of Guangling, at the capital; by the eastern road he was to meet Changsun Han at the enemy camp.

literal: Fifth month, day dingwei: halted in the desert, left the baggage train, light horse with spare mounts reached Lishui; the Rouran were terrified, burned their lodges, and vanished west.
idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the fifth month he halted in the desert, left the baggage, and with light horse and remounts reached Lishui; the Rouran were terrified, burned their camps, and fled west without trace.

literal: The matter is fully set forth in the Rouran treatise.
idiomatic: The full account is in the treatise on the Rouran.

literal: That month Helian Ding came to raid Tongwan, went east to Houni city and returned.
idiomatic: That month Helian Ding raided Tongwan, reached Houni city in the east, and withdrew.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: the imperial carriage turned east.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the court turned east.

literal: At Heishan the armies' stores were reviewed and distributed to princes, dukes, and officers and soldiers, each according to merit.
idiomatic: At Heishan the booty was counted and divided among princes, dukes, and troops, each as earned.

literal: Eighth month: because the eastern Gaoche were encamped at Sini marsh, an edict that Left Vice Director An Yuan was to lead more than ten thousand horse against them.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, because eastern Gaoche were camped at Sini marsh, he ordered An Yuan, Left Vice Director, with more than ten thousand horse against them.

literal: The matter is fully set forth in the Rouran treatise.
idiomatic: The full account is in the treatise on the Rouran.

literal: Winter, tenth month: the army returned in triumph to the capital and reported at the ancestral temple.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter the army returned in triumph to the capital and reported to the ancestral temple.

literal: New subjects were arrayed south of the desert, east to Ruyuan, west to Wuyuan and Yinshan, three thousand li in all.
idiomatic: New subjects were settled south of the desert from Ruyuan in the east to Wuyuan and Yinshan in the west, three thousand li in all.

literal: An edict that Chancellor Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han, Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie, Left Vice Director An Yuan, and Palace Attendant Gu Bi were to garrison and pacify them.
idiomatic: He ordered Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang and Chancellor, Liu Jie, Director of the Masters of Writing, An Yuan, Left Vice Director, and Gu Bi, Palace Attendant, to garrison and pacify them.

literal: Eleventh month: toured west on a hunt, hunted on Hexi, reached Zuoshan and returned.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month he hunted west in Hexi, reached Zuoshan, and returned.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day jiazi: traveled to Yunzhong.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the jiazi day, he went to Yunzhong.

literal: More than ten thousand Tiele households rebelled and fled.
idiomatic: More than ten thousand Tiele households rebelled and fled.

literal: An edict that Director of the Masters of Writing Feng Tie was to pursue and destroy them.
idiomatic: He ordered Feng Tie of the Masters of Writing to pursue and destroy them.

literal: Fifth month, day wuxu, edict: "A gentleman's conduct: at home he must be filial, at court loyal—then his person is honored in his age and his name praised by later generations.
idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the fifth month an edict declared: "A man's conduct should be filial at home and loyal at court; only then is he honored in his time and remembered after."

literal: Recently Director Feng Tie cut down fugitives; among the officers and soldiers under his command were those who gave their utmost loyalty and perished in the service—now all are posthumously enfeoffed with noble rank;
idiomatic: "Lately Feng Tie of the Masters of Writing destroyed fugitives. Officers and men who died in loyal service shall now receive posthumous ranks;

literal: there were those who braved blades and hardship to offer themselves—advancement in rank according to merit;
idiomatic: those who braved blades and hardship shall be advanced by merit;

literal: there were those who deliberately violated military law and privately left their banners—execution by military law.
idiomatic: those who deliberately broke military law and left their units shall die by military law.

literal: Merit receives reward, crime receives punishment—the constant rule of the state cannot for a moment be abandoned.
idiomatic: "Merit is rewarded and crime punished—the state's constant rule must not lapse even for a moment."

literal: From now on the unworthy may reform themselves.
idiomatic: "From now on the unworthy may reform themselves."

literal: Proclaim this inside and outside so all may hear and know.
idiomatic: "Let this be proclaimed within and without until all have heard."

literal: " Sixth month: an edict that General Who Pacifies the South, Acting Prince of Danyang Taipi, was to garrison on the river; Sima Chuzhi was made General Who Pacifies the South, Prince of Langye, and garrisoned Yingchuan.
idiomatic: In the sixth month he ordered Taipi, General Who Pacifies the South and acting Prince of Danyang, to garrison on the river, and made Sima Chuzhi General Who Pacifies the South and Prince of Langye, garrisoning Yingchuan.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jihai, edict: "In former times Taizu raised order amid chaos and institutions were first drafted; Taizong followed along and had no leisure to revise; military and civil offices even stood vacant.
idiomatic: On the jihai day of the seventh month of autumn an edict said: "Taizu, raising order from chaos, first drafted institutions; Taizong followed but had no time to revise them, and military and civil posts even stood empty."

literal: Now generals on campaign, princes and dukes bearing credentials on distant frontiers, are permitted to open offices and recruit;
idiomatic: "Now campaigning generals and princes and dukes with credentials on distant frontiers may open offices and recruit;

literal: next, increase the number of clerks.
idiomatic: next, increase clerical staff."

literal: " Day gengzi: Director of the Grand Messenger Office Du Chao was given credentials, made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Ji, Ding, and Xiang provinces, Acting General Who Conquers the South, Grand Preceptor, advanced to prince, garrisoned Ye, and made coordinator of all armies.
idiomatic: On the gengzi day Du Chao, Director of the Grand Messenger Office, received credentials as commander of armies in Ji, Ding, and Xiang, acting General Who Conquers the South and Grand Preceptor, was raised to princely rank, garrisoned Ye, and coordinated all armies.

literal: Eighth month: bandits in Qinghe killed the governor.
idiomatic: In the eighth month bandits in Qinghe killed the governor.

literal: Liu Yilong's general Dao Yanzhi entered the river from Qingshui and sailed upstream west.
idiomatic: Dao Yanzhi, general to Liu Yilong, entered the Yellow River from Qingshui and sailed upstream west.

literal: The Emperor, because Henan had few troops, ordered the four garrisons taken under central command.
idiomatic: Because Henan had few troops, the emperor put the four frontier garrisons under central command.

literal: Thereupon troops were drilled for a western campaign.
idiomatic: He then drilled the army for a western expedition.

literal: Day bingyin: Dao Yanzhi sent generals across the river to attack Yebai; Champion General An Gu directed the armies, defeated them, beheaded more than five thousand, and very many drowned.
idiomatic: On the bingyin day Yanzhi sent generals across the river against Yebai; An Gu, Champion General, led the armies, broke them, took more than five thousand heads, and drowned many more.

literal: Day jiaxu: traveled to Nangong and hunted on Nanshan.
idiomatic: On the jiaxu day he went to Nangong and hunted on Nanshan.

literal: Day wuyin: an edict that General Who Conquers the West Changsun Daosheng was to garrison on the river.
idiomatic: On the wuyin day he ordered Changsun Daosheng, General Who Conquers the West, to garrison on the river.

literal: Ninth month, day jichou: Helian Ding sent his younger brother Wei Yi to raid Fucheng on behalf of Dai; General Who Pacifies the West, Duke of Shiping Wei Gui and others led the armies against them, captured the bandit general Wang Bei, killed more than ten thousand, and Wei Yi fled.
idiomatic: On the jichou day of the ninth month Ding sent his brother Wei Yi to raid Fucheng for Dai; Wei Gui, General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Shiping, and others attacked, took the rebel general Wang Bei, killed more than ten thousand, and Wei Yi fled.

literal: Day guimao: the temple of Empress Mi was established at Ye.
idiomatic: On the guimao day the temple of Empress Mi was founded at Ye.

literal: Day jiachen: traveled to Tongwan and then campaigned against Pingliang.
idiomatic: On the jiachen day he went to Tongwan and marched on Pingliang.

literal: Winter, tenth month, day gengshen: Dao Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde set guards along the river and withdrew to defend Dongping.
idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the tenth month of winter Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde posted guards along the river and fell back to Dongping.

literal: Day yihai: Champion General An Gu crossed the river and attacked Luoyang; day bingzi, took it, captured twenty of Yilong's generals, and beheaded five thousand.
idiomatic: On the yihai day An Gu, Champion General, crossed the river and attacked Luoyang; on the bingzi day he took it, captured twenty of Yilong's generals, and beheaded five thousand.

literal: At that time the armies of Hebei gathered at Qinv Ford; Yanzhi feared a southern crossing and sent General Wang Panlong upstream to seize government boats; Du Chao, General Who Conquers the South, and others defeated and beheaded him.
idiomatic: The armies of Hebei gathered at Qinv Ford; fearing a southern crossing, Yanzhi sent Wang Panlong upstream to seize government boats; Du Chao, General Who Conquers the South, and others defeated and killed him.

literal: Day xinsi: An Gu pacified Hubao; Yilong's Inspector of Sizhou Yin Chong fell from the wall and died.
idiomatic: On the xinsi day An Gu took Hubao; Yin Chong, Yilong's inspector of Sizhou, fell from the wall and died.

literal: Eleventh month, day yiyou: the imperial carriage reached Pingliang.
idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the eleventh month the court reached Pingliang.

literal: Earlier Helian Ding with tens of thousands of men had gone east to hold Fucheng; he left his younger brother Duke of Shanggu Sheyu and Duke of Guangyang Duluo to guard the city.
idiomatic: Earlier Ding had gone east to Fucheng with tens of thousands; he left his brothers Sheyu, Duke of Shanggu, and Duluo, Duke of Guangyang, to hold the city.

literal: The Emperor reached Pingliang, mounted the north plateau, and had Helian Chang summon them; Sheyu did not submit.
idiomatic: The emperor reached Pingliang, mounted the north plateau, and had Helian Chang summon them; Sheyu refused.

literal: An edict that General Who Pacifies the West Gu Bi and others were to attack Anding and assault Pingliang.
idiomatic: He ordered Gu Bi, General Who Pacifies the West, and others to attack Anding and besiege Pingliang.

literal: Ding heard, abandoned Fucheng, entered Anding, and himself led thirty thousand foot and horse from Chunqu plain to relieve Pingliang; he met Bi, Bi struck him, killed several thousand, and Ding turned back in flight.
idiomatic: Ding heard, abandoned Fucheng, entered Anding, and led thirty thousand foot and horse from Chunqu plain to relieve Pingliang; he met Bi, who struck him, killed several thousand, and Ding fled back.

literal: An edict that the armies were to surround on all four sides.
idiomatic: He ordered the armies to invest the city on all sides.

literal: Day jiawu: Marquis of Shouguang Shusun Jian and Duke of Runan Changsun Daosheng crossed the river; Dao Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde went from Qing into Ji and fled east to Qingzhou; Zhu Lingxiu, Yilong's governor of Yanzhou, abandoned Xuchang and fled south to Hulu.
idiomatic: On the jiawu day Shusun Jian, Marquis of Shouguang, and Changsun Daosheng, Duke of Runan, crossed the river; Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde fled east from Qing and Ji to Qingzhou; Zhu Lingxiu, Yilong's governor of Yanzhou, abandoned Xuchang and fled south to Hulu.

literal: Day dingyou: Ding lacked water and led his host down from the high ground; an edict that Martial Guard General Qiu Juan was to strike him; Ding's host was utterly routed and more than ten thousand died.
idiomatic: On the dingyou day Ding ran short of water and led his men down from the heights; the emperor ordered Qiu Juan, Martial Guard General, to strike; Ding's army broke and more than ten thousand died.

literal: Ding was gravely wounded and fled alone on horseback.
idiomatic: Ding was badly wounded and fled alone on horseback.

literal: Captured Ding's younger brother Duke of Danyang Wushiba, Duke of Wuling Tugu, and more than a hundred dukes and marquises.
idiomatic: They took Ding's brother Wushiba, Duke of Danyang, Tugu, Duke of Wuling, and more than a hundred dukes and marquises.

literal: That day the generals pressed the victory and advanced; Anding was then taken.
idiomatic: That day the generals pressed the victory and took Anding.

literal: Ding's cousin Duke of Dongping Yisheng abandoned the city and fled to Chang'an, plundering several thousand households, then fled west to Shanggui.
idiomatic: Ding's cousin Yisheng, Duke of Dongping, abandoned the city, fled to Chang'an, plundered several thousand households, and fled west to Shanggui.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: Day wuxu: Shusun Jian utterly defeated Zhu Lingxiu at Hulu, killing and capturing more than five thousand.
idiomatic: On the wuxu day Shusun Jian broke Zhu Lingxiu at Hulu and killed or captured more than five thousand.

literal: Day jihai: the Emperor visited Anding, took Qifu Chipo's hostage and Ding's chariots and banners, registered captives and livestock, and distributed to the officers and soldiers, each according to merit.
idiomatic: On the jihai day the emperor visited Anding, took Qifu Chipo's hostage and Ding's chariots and banners, tallied captives and herds, and divided them among the troops, each as earned.

literal: Day gengzi: the Emperor returned from Anding to Pingliang and dug trenches to invest the city.
idiomatic: On the gengzi day he returned from Anding to Pingliang and dug trenches to besiege it.

literal: Traveled to Niucheng, comforted those newly submitted, pardoned the people of Qin and Yong, and granted seven years' remission of levies.
idiomatic: He went to Niucheng, reassured the newly submitted, pardoned the people of Qin and Yong, and remitted levies for seven years.

literal: Defenders and officers and soldiers of Longxi, several thousand, came to surrender.
idiomatic: Several thousand defenders and soldiers of Longxi surrendered.

literal: Day xinchou: Champion General An Gu led the armies to attack Huatai.
idiomatic: On the xinchou day An Gu, Champion General, led the armies against Huatai.

literal: Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi defeated Liu Yilong's general at Changshe.
idiomatic: Sima Chuzhi, Prince of Langye, defeated a general of Liu Yilong at Changshe.
